title: THERM-201 Protective Shutdown Runbook
author: ENG-104
summary: Symptoms: pack temperature rises over minutes to hours while discharging, cooling fan tach falls to zero, THERM-110 warns, then THERM-201 opens the contactors and the battery goes offline. Steps: 1) Save the two-hour temperature trace. 2) Confirm fan tach. 3) If tach is zero and temperature is still rising, replace the cooling fan. 4) Do not raise the Temperature Threshold to clear THERM-201. 5) Recommission only after the new fan runs. Use this runbook for DEV-001. Do not use it for a drifting sensor.

title: Field Configuration Guide: Thermal Thresholds
author: ENG-118
summary: This guide conflicts with the THERM-201 Protective Shutdown Runbook. It tells the field to raise Temperature Threshold by 10 C when THERM-201 trips, and it treats cooling fan replacement as optional if the pack can be started again. The runbook forbids that threshold change. Both documents are Published. Engineering should follow the runbook, not this guide, until this guide is withdrawn.

title: Firmware 4.2.1 Release Note
author: ENG-110
summary: Previous stable release. Fixed 200 ms heartbeat, uncompressed telemetry frames, communication timeout handled in the gateway task. Known issues: none critical. 4.2.1 does not contain the COM-214 regression. It remains the rollback target from 4.3.0.

title: Firmware 4.3.0 Release Note
author: ENG-110
summary: What changed from 4.2.1: the fixed heartbeat was replaced with an adaptive heartbeat, telemetry frames were compressed, and communication timeout handling moved from the gateway task into the shared session layer. Known issue: the new state machine drops a healthy session when one-way latency exceeds 120 ms (COM-214, FW-210). Signal strength is not affected. Rollout status: halted. Fix is 4.3.1.

title: Firmware 4.3.1 Release Note
author: ENG-110
summary: 4.3.1 keeps compressed telemetry and restores the 4.2.1 heartbeat timing. It resolves COM-214 and the FW-210 signature introduced in 4.3.0. Hardware-in-loop test: 4.3.0 drops the session at 180 ms induced latency; 4.3.1 and 4.2.1 stay up.

title: Failure Analysis: 4.3.0 Communications Regression
author: ENG-110
summary: Symptoms started within hours of the 4.3.0 install: latency stepped from about 30 ms to above 300 ms and COM-214 fired. RSSI stayed near -64 dBm. Peers that stayed on 4.2.1 did not fail. Rollback to 4.2.1 or upgrade to 4.3.1 clears the symptom. A radio replacement does not.

title: COM-101 Gateway Link Loss Diagnostic Procedure
author: ENG-104
summary: Symptoms: latency rises and signal strength falls together, telemetry gaps appear, then the gateway goes offline. Steps: 1) Plot latency and RSSI on the same axis. 2) If both degrade, inspect the antenna, cable, and radio. 3) If only latency rises and RSSI is steady, stop and check for the 4.3.0 COM-214 regression instead. The Owl Hollow gateway is the radio-path example.

title: COM-214 Heartbeat Session Drop Diagnostic Procedure
author: ENG-110
summary: Symptoms: COM-214 or FW-210 shortly after a 4.3.0 install, latency high, signal strength unchanged. Steps: 1) Read firmware history. 2) Confirm the first fault is after the 4.3.0 installed_at. 3) Roll back to 4.2.1 or upgrade to 4.3.1. 4) Do not replace the radio.

title: Distinguishing Pack Thermal Rise from Temperature-Sensor Drift
author: ENG-118
summary: Real thermal failure example is DEV-001: temperature rises over hours while discharging, fan tach is zero, voltage sags slightly, THERM-201 trips, and the pack goes offline. There is no snap-back. Sensor drift example is DEV-037: temperature climbs for days while current and voltage stay normal, THERM-110 and THERM-155 fire, the pack stays online, and the reading snaps back to about 28 C in one sample after the sensor is replaced. Do not replace a cooling fan for the drift case. Do not raise the threshold for the real shutdown.

title: Inverter Power Limit Configuration Guide
author: ENG-125
summary: Symptoms of a mismatched Inverter Power Limit: afternoon power flatlines at the configured cap, INV-360 repeats, and the grid is healthy. Steps: 1) Open device_configuration. 2) A Mismatch row has parameter_value different from expected_value. The Limestone case was 75 kW versus expected 90 kW. 3) Restore the expected value. 4) Confirm the next discharge exceeds the old cap. The latest row for that inverter is the corrected 90 kW value.

title: Failure Analysis: BAT-204 on Hardware Revision HW-C
author: ENG-125
summary: Three packs at three sites, all hardware revision HW-C, raised BAT-204 during discharge above 70 kW. Voltage swung outside 740 to 770 V before the fault. Firmware and current limits were not common. Confirmed cause: power-module busbar torque below spec. Temporary mitigation is a 60 kW discharge cap.

title: Proactive Watchlist: Early Degradation Signals
author: ENG-101
summary: Investigate these while they are still online: a pack whose temperature sits near 40 C without approaching the 60 C trip, a gateway whose latency climbs through roughly 140 ms with stable RSSI and which is not on firmware 4.3.0, and a pack with isolated BMS-218 watchdog restarts that recovers each time. These are early warnings, not the Copper Elm shutdown and not the 4.3.0 regression.

title: Open Investigation Note: Unexpected SOC Step
author: ENG-101
summary: INC-008 on DEV-045 remains under investigation. The symptom is an SOC step of about 50 points while current and power at that sample were near zero. Unconfirmed hypotheses are SOC estimator bias, current-sensor offset, and standby parasitic load. None is confirmed. Firmware is 4.2.1, matching healthy peers. Do not write a confirmed cause into the ticket.

title: Grid Frequency Excursion and Inverter Latch Runbook
author: ENG-110
summary: Symptoms: grid frequency leaves 59.5 to 60.5 Hz, inverter power falls, then frequency returns and power stays at zero because INV-201 latches. Steps: 1) Confirm the frequency peak on the inverter trace. 2) If the grid was really outside the band, do not replace the power module. 3) Reset only with a supervised procedure. The Lantern Field event peaked at 61.28 Hz.

title: Pack, Inverter, and Gateway Data Path
author: ENG-110
summary: The BMS publishes pack telemetry to the site gateway. The inverter publishes AC power, grid voltage, and grid frequency. The gateway heartbeats to the collector. Firmware 4.2.1 heartbeats from the gateway task. Firmware 4.3.0 moved that work into a shared session layer. Firmware 4.3.1 keeps the session layer and restores 4.2.1 timing. Energy controllers and sensors were not built on 4.3.0.

title: Normal Operating Envelopes
author: ENG-125
summary: Pack temperature 24 to 35 C in normal weather. Pack voltage about 740 to 770 V. Grid frequency 59.95 to 60.05 Hz outside of a disturbance. Heartbeat latency about 15 to 50 ms. RSSI about -75 to -55 dBm. Evening inverter peaks near the 90 kW rating unless a configuration cap is present. SOC moves with charge and discharge energy.

title: Arroyo-200 and Ledge-200 Installation Guide
author: ENG-125
summary: Both pack models are 200 kWh. HW-C power modules need a recorded busbar torque at installation. Skip the torque record and BAT-204 is the likely field result under discharge above 70 kW. HW-A packs stay on firmware 4.1.4 or 4.2.1. 4.3.x requires HW-B or later.

title: Similar Shutdowns, Different Causes
author: ENG-104
summary: Two incidents share the symptom: the main contactor opened during a routine discharge, with no thermal alarm and no recent firmware change. INC-009 was a failed contactor coil driver (coil current zero, REL-204). INC-010 was an open precharge resistor (coil current present, DC bus did not rise, REL-210). Do not copy the first repair onto the second symptom.

title: Configuration Mismatch Troubleshooting Guide
author: ENG-125
summary: A row with configuration_status Mismatch has parameter_value different from expected_value. Matching rows are equal. Live examples in this snapshot include SOC Maximum 75 versus expected 90, Communication Timeout 8 s versus 30 s, and Grid Voltage Limit 492 V versus 504 V. The Limestone inverter also keeps the historical 75 kW row; its later row is the corrected 90 kW value.

title: Repeated Fault Investigation Procedure
author: ENG-125
summary: When the same error code appears at several sites, group by hardware revision, firmware, configuration, and operating condition before replacing parts. The HW-C BAT-204 cluster matched on revision and on discharge above 70 kW, not on firmware. The sister INV-305 cases matched on DC bus capacitor ESR.

title: Superseded Envelope Table
author: ENG-118
summary: Superseded by Normal Operating Envelopes 2.0. The old table allowed pack temperature up to 45 C as normal. The current spec treats sustained temperature near 40 C as an early warning, not as a normal band.

title: BAT-101 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: BAT-101 Cell delta elevated during charge. Severity Warning. One cell group is more than 30 mV from the pack median while charging. Likely causes: Uneven cell aging; balancer duty cycle too low; loose sense lead. Steps: 1) Compare group voltages in the BMS snapshot. 2) Confirm the balancer is running. 3) Reseat the sense harness if the delta is on one channel only. Related component: Voltage Sensor. Firmware fix: none.

title: BAT-102 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: BAT-102 Charge complete. Severity Info. The pack reached the configured SOC maximum and charge current tapered to standby. Likely causes: Normal end of charge. Steps: 1) Confirm SOC matches the coulomb count. 2) No field action if the taper was controlled. Related component: BMS. Firmware fix: none.

title: BAT-118 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: BAT-118 SOC residual above estimate band. Severity Warning. The SOC estimator and the coulomb counter differ by more than 8 points. Likely causes: Current sensor offset; estimator bias after a partial cycle; stale voltage reference. Steps: 1) Rest the pack for 20 minutes and compare open-circuit voltage to SOC. 2) Check current-sensor zero. 3) Do not recalibrate until the residual repeats. Related component: Current Sensor. Firmware fix: none.

title: BAT-217 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: BAT-217 Charge current above setpoint. Severity Warning. Charge current exceeded the configured max for one sample and then returned. Likely causes: Transient setpoint overshoot; current sensor spike; charger handshake glitch. Steps: 1) Check whether the spike lasted more than one sample. 2) Compare current sensor to the inverter DC reading. 3) Clear if it does not repeat. Related component: Current Sensor. Firmware fix: none.

title: BMS-104 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: BMS-104 Cell balancing active. Severity Info. The BMS enabled passive balancing on one or more cell groups. Likely causes: Normal balancing after a charge. Steps: 1) Confirm balance current is inside the BMS spec. 2) No action if group delta is falling. Related component: BMS. Firmware fix: none.

title: BMS-210 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: BMS-210 BMS temperature channels disagree. Severity Warning. Two BMS temperature channels differ by more than 6 C while current is below 10 A. Likely causes: Sensor drift; harness resistance; real local hotspot. Steps: 1) Compare both channels to the pack current. 2) A drift case stays high at zero current. 3) A hotspot rises with current. Related component: Temperature Sensor. Firmware fix: none.

title: BMS-301 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: BMS-301 Cell voltage sense channel stale. Severity Error. A voltage sense channel missed three updates. Likely causes: Sense harness; BMS analog front end; connector fretting. Steps: 1) Identify the stale channel. 2) Swap the sense lead to a known-good port if the procedure allows. 3) Replace the harness before the BMS board. Related component: Voltage Sensor. Firmware fix: none.

title: BMS-330 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: BMS-330 BMS safety latch. Severity Critical. The BMS latched a safety output and opened the contactors. Likely causes: Real protection event; failed safety input; firmware latch bug. Steps: 1) Read the latch source bit. 2) Do not clear the latch until telemetry around the bit is saved. Related component: BMS. Firmware fix: none.

title: INV-109 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: INV-109 Inverter online. Severity Info. The inverter completed precharge and closed its AC contactor. Likely causes: Normal start. Steps: 1) Confirm grid voltage and frequency are inside limits. 2) No action. Related component: Inverter Controller. Firmware fix: none.

title: INV-214 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: INV-214 Inverter thermal derate. Severity Warning. AC output was reduced because the inverter heat sink crossed the derate threshold. Likely causes: Blocked airflow; high ambient; fan wear. Steps: 1) Compare heat-sink temperature to power. 2) Inspect the inverter fan. 3) Derate is expected only above the configured temperature threshold. Related component: Cooling Fan. Firmware fix: none.

title: INV-250 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: INV-250 Restart delay active. Severity Warning. The inverter is waiting out the configured restart delay before reconnecting. Likely causes: Recent trip; configured delay; operator command. Steps: 1) Read the delay timer. 2) Confirm the delay matches the approved configuration. Related component: Inverter Controller. Firmware fix: none.

title: INV-318 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: INV-318 AC overvoltage ride-through. Severity Warning. Grid voltage entered the ride-through band and the inverter stayed online. Likely causes: Utility switching; tap changer; local capacitor switching. Steps: 1) Record the voltage peak and duration. 2) No inverter repair if the event stayed inside the ride-through curve. Related component: Inverter Controller. Firmware fix: none.

title: INV-402 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: INV-402 Inverter output collapsed. Severity Error. AC power fell by more than 50 kW in one sample while the grid was inside normal limits. Likely causes: Phase module fault; gate-driver undervoltage; DC input sag. Steps: 1) Compare grid voltage and DC bus at the drop. 2) If the grid is normal and the bus sags, inspect the power module. 3) Open a hardware ticket if the output stays down. Related component: Power Module. Firmware fix: none.

title: INV-415 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: INV-415 Inverter hardware trip. Severity Critical. A hardware comparator tripped the inverter faster than the software loop. Likely causes: Desaturation; overcurrent; failed gate driver. Steps: 1) Do not restart more than once. 2) Capture the hardware trip code. 3) Replace the power module if desaturation is set. Related component: Power Module. Firmware fix: none.

title: COM-090 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: COM-090 Link quality nominal. Severity Info. Heartbeat latency and signal strength are inside the nominal band. Likely causes: Normal operation. Steps: 1) No action. Related component: Communication Module. Firmware fix: none.

title: COM-240 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: COM-240 Compressed telemetry frames enabled. Severity Info. The gateway is sending the compressed frame format introduced in 4.3.0. Likely causes: Firmware feature. Steps: 1) Confirm the collector accepts compressed frames. 2) No fault action. Related component: Communication Module. Firmware fix: none.

title: GRID-118 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: GRID-118 Grid voltage outside preferred band. Severity Warning. Grid voltage left the preferred band but stayed inside the trip limits. Likely causes: Utility regulation; local switching. Steps: 1) Record duration. 2) Compare with the neighboring site. 3) No inverter repair for a shared grid dip. Related component: Voltage Sensor. Firmware fix: none.

title: GRID-201 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: GRID-201 Grid nominal. Severity Info. Grid voltage and frequency returned to the nominal band. Likely causes: Normal recovery. Steps: 1) No action. Related component: Inverter Controller. Firmware fix: none.

title: GRID-310 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: GRID-310 Grid disconnect. Severity Critical. The inverter opened the AC contactor because the grid stayed outside limits past the ride-through timer. Likely causes: Sustained grid disturbance; failed grid relay. Steps: 1) Save the pre-trip waveform. 2) Reclose only after the grid is inside limits for the restart delay. Related component: Relay. Firmware fix: none.

title: GW-101 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: GW-101 Gateway CPU elevated. Severity Warning. Gateway CPU stayed above 80 percent for 10 minutes. Likely causes: Firmware 4.4.0 lab build; log flood; retry storm. Steps: 1) Check the firmware version. 2) Confirm this is not a 4.3.0 heartbeat storm. 3) Capture a CPU profile before replacing hardware. Related component: Gateway. Firmware fix: none.

title: GW-140 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: GW-140 Gateway restart loop. Severity Error. The gateway rebooted more than three times in an hour. Likely causes: Power supply; firmware crash; watchdog. Steps: 1) Read the reboot reason. 2) Check the supply rail. 3) Hold the device out of the firmware rollout if the reboot reason is a panic. Related component: Gateway. Firmware fix: none.

title: FW-104 Quick Diagnostic Card
author: ENG-118
summary: FW-104 Firmware bank verified. Severity Info. The inactive firmware bank signature matched the release manifest. Likely causes: Normal update pre-check. Steps: 1) No action. Related component: Communication Module. Firmware fix: none.

title: Cooling Fan Tach Check
author: ENG-125
summary: Check cooling fan tach before changing a temperature threshold. A zero tach with rising temperature means replace the fan.

title: HW-C Busbar Torque Record
author: ENG-125
summary: Record busbar torque on every HW-C power module at installation. Low torque shows up later as BAT-204 under discharge.

title: Heartbeat Timing Comparison
author: ENG-125
summary: 4.2.1 uses a fixed heartbeat. 4.3.0 drops sessions above 120 ms. 4.3.1 restores the 4.2.1 timing and keeps compressed frames.

title: Radio Path versus Heartbeat Regression
author: ENG-125
summary: If latency and signal strength both move, inspect the radio. If only latency moves and the image is 4.3.0, treat it as the heartbeat regression.

title: Inverter Power Limit Audit
author: ENG-125
summary: Compare parameter_value with expected_value. A mismatch row is not a hardware fault until the values are equal and the cap remains.

title: Sensor Replacement Note
author: ENG-125
summary: A drifting temperature sensor snaps back in one sample after replacement. A real thermal shutdown does not.

title: Contactor Coil versus Precharge
author: ENG-125
summary: Zero coil current points at the coil driver. Coil current with no DC bus rise points at the precharge resistor.

title: Grid Latch Reset Procedure
author: ENG-125
summary: After a real frequency excursion, leave the inverter latch set until a supervised reset. Do not swap the power module for the grid event.

title: DC Bus Capacitor ESR Check
author: ENG-125
summary: Sister inverters with the same ripple signature share a DC bus capacitor ESR rise. Compare them before blaming the grid.

title: Watchdog Restart Counting
author: ENG-125
summary: Count BMS-218 restarts in 24 hours. One restart can be a supply dip. More than three in a day is an escalation.

title: Gateway CPU Profile Request
author: ENG-125
summary: Capture a CPU profile before replacing a gateway that shows a short CPU blip. A 4.4.0 lab image is not approved for the field.

title: SOC Step Investigation Checklist
author: ENG-125
summary: When SOC steps without matching current, list estimator bias, current-sensor offset, and standby load as hypotheses. Do not confirm one from a single sample.

title: Proactive Temperature Watch
author: ENG-125
summary: A pack that sits near 40 C and stays online is an early warning. It is not a THERM-201 shutdown.

title: Communication Timeout Template
author: ENG-125
summary: The approved communication timeout is 30 s. A running value of 8 s is a mismatch and should be restored through a change record.

title: Release Bank Verification
author: ENG-125
summary: FW-104 means the inactive bank matched the manifest. It is an informational check, not a fault.
